concepts.note: Planck's law fits the observed spectrum and avoids the ultraviolet catastrophe.
concepts.title: Blackbody radiation law

concepts.note: The classical Rayleigh–Jeans law predicts divergent energy at short wavelengths.
concepts.title: Ultraviolet catastrophe

concepts.note: Energy exchange occurs in units E = hν, where ν is frequency.
concepts.title: Energy quantization

concepts.note: h ≈ 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s sets the quantum of action.
concepts.title: Planck constant

subtopics.note: Planck explained blackbody radiation by assuming oscillator energies are emitted or absorbed in discrete quanta E = hν, introducing the Planck constant h.
subtopics.title: Planck quantum

concepts.note: Electrons occupy discrete orbits without radiating.
concepts.title: Stationary states

concepts.note: Transition energies reproduce the Balmer and Lyman series.
concepts.title: Hydrogen spectrum

concepts.note: a₀ = 4πε₀ħ²/(m_e e²) ≈ 0.529 Å sets atomic size.
concepts.title: Bohr radius

concepts.note: Quantum predictions approach classical physics for large n.
concepts.title: Correspondence principle

subtopics.note: Bohr proposed quantized stationary electron orbits with angular momentum L = nħ, with radiation emitted only in transitions hν = E_i − E_f.
subtopics.title: Bohr atom

concepts.note: Observables are noncommuting matrices; [x,p] = iħ.
concepts.title: Heisenberg matrix mechanics

concepts.note: The wavefunction evolves according to iħ∂ψ/∂t = Ĥψ.
concepts.title: Schrödinger equation

concepts.note: |ψ|² gives the probability density for measurement outcomes.
concepts.title: Born probability rule

concepts.note: Dirac and Jordan formalized the equivalence of matrix and wave mechanics.
concepts.title: Transformation theory

subtopics.note: Heisenberg's matrix mechanics (1925) and Schrödinger's wave mechanics (1926) gave two equivalent formulations of quantum mechanics. The wave equation is iħ∂ψ/∂t = Ĥψ.
subtopics.title: Matrix and wave mechanics

concepts.note: Δx Δp ≥ ħ/2 limits simultaneous knowledge.
concepts.title: Position-momentum uncertainty

concepts.note: ΔE Δt ≳ ħ/2 constrains lifetime and energy spread, though its interpretation is subtle.
concepts.title: Energy-time uncertainty

concepts.note: Bohr argued wave and particle descriptions are complementary, not simultaneously applicable.
concepts.title: Complementarity

concepts.note: Measurement inevitably disturbs conjugate variables in the Copenhagen view.
concepts.title: Measurement disturbance

subtopics.note: Heisenberg showed that noncommuting observables cannot both be sharply defined, with Δx Δp ≥ ħ/2.
subtopics.title: Uncertainty principle

concepts.note: The first-order equation treats space and time on equal footing.
concepts.title: Relativistic wave equation

concepts.note: The four-component spinor automatically includes electron spin.
concepts.title: Spin-1/2

concepts.note: The equation has negative-energy solutions interpreted as positrons, discovered in 1932.
concepts.title: Antimatter prediction

concepts.note: Hole theory interpreted negative-energy states as antiparticles.
concepts.title: Dirac sea

subtopics.note: Dirac's relativistic wave equation iħ∂ψ/∂t = (cα·p + βmc²)ψ predicted spin-1/2 electrons and antimatter.
subtopics.title: Dirac equation

concepts.note: The 1935 argument used entangled positions and momenta to question completeness.
concepts.title: EPR paradox

concepts.note: Schrödinger coined the term for nonseparable correlations between subsystems.
concepts.title: Quantum entanglement

concepts.note: Local hidden-variable correlations must satisfy bounds that quantum entanglement violates.
concepts.title: Bell inequality

concepts.note: The 1969 extension made Bell's theorem experimentally testable.
concepts.title: CHSH inequality

subtopics.note: Einstein, Podolsky and Rosen argued in 1935 that quantum mechanics is incomplete; Bell showed in 1964 that any local hidden-variable theory obeys inequalities violated by entangled states.
subtopics.title: Entanglement and Bell's theorem

concepts.note: The 1947 measurement of hydrogen 2S–2P splitting stimulated QED.
concepts.title: Lamb shift

concepts.note: Divergent parameters are absorbed into physical mass and charge.
concepts.title: Renormalization

concepts.note: Graphical perturbation rules organize QED scattering amplitudes.
concepts.title: Feynman diagrams

concepts.note: QED predicts g ≈ 2.0023 for the electron, matching experiment.
concepts.title: Anomalous magnetic moment

subtopics.note: Feynman, Schwinger and Tomonaga developed covariant QED calculations, and Dyson showed how to renormalize infinities into measured mass and charge. The electron anomalous moment a_e = (g − 2)/2 ≈ α/(2π) became a precision test.
subtopics.title: QED renormalization

concepts.note: Non-Abelian gauge fields have nonlinear self-interactions.
concepts.title: Yang-Mills theory

concepts.note: Demanding invariance under spacetime-dependent transformations generates gauge interactions.
concepts.title: Local gauge invariance

concepts.note: The f^{abc} term makes gauge bosons carry gauge charge.
concepts.title: Non-Abelian field strength

concepts.note: Unbroken gauge symmetry predicts massless bosons, motivating spontaneous symmetry breaking in the 1960s.
concepts.title: Gauge boson masses

subtopics.note: Yang and Mills generalized local U(1) gauge invariance to non-Abelian SU(2), introducing self-interacting gauge bosons. The field strength is F^a_{μν} = ∂_μ A^a_ν − ∂_ν A^a_μ + g f^{abc} A^b_μ A^c_ν.
subtopics.title: Gauge field theory
